concerns.text: "The difference in epidemic threshold between the topology‑only model and the spatially constrained model is measured against the null distribution" does not specify a quantitative metric or decision threshold (e.g., absolute difference, effect size, or p‑value). Without a concrete measurable target the criterion cannot be automatically evaluated.

"The robustness of the findings is measured by the variation in the epidemic threshold across the sensitivity sweep of λ ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}" lacks a definition of “variation” (range, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, etc.) and any acceptable bound, making it untestable.

The scenario requires the spatial model’s peak‑infection reduction to exceed the reduction observed in the synthetic‑control (MDS) condition, yet the synthetic‑control is only generated when coordinates are missing (FR‑011). If the dataset provides real coordinates, the synthetic‑control does not exist, rendering the acceptance condition unreachable.

FR‑007 mandates a hard 6‑hour runtime limit and dynamic adjustment of simulation count or network size, but does not define a measurable trigger (e.g., “if elapsed time > 5 h reduce iterations by 50 %”). Without a precise rule the behavior cannot be verified.
FR‑011 duplicates FR‑001’s description of MDS‑generated coordinates, creating potential ambiguity about when synthetic coordinates are produced and how they are used as a control.
